newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescuers find ninth body from Australia landslide.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers find ninth body from Australia landslide.

text.p: Rescuers on Sunday found a ninth body in the debris of a three-day-old landslide at an Australian ski resort as bad weather loomed as a major threat to the rescue effort.

The weather has so far smiled on the rescue crews who have worked beneath near-cloudless skies to miraculously recover one survivor, ski instructor Stuart Diver, as well as four of nine dead bodies now unearthed from the hillside at Thredbo village.
The ninth body was found on Sunday morning after a night of triumph in pulling Diver, 27, from the rubble quickly returned to frustration for exhausted rescue crews working under lights.
They were forced several times to suspend their efforts after the rubble shifted ominously, threatening to send debris crashing further down the steep slope.
After three and a half days of fine weather, police chief superintendent Charlie Sanderson expressed fears on Sunday morning that rain clouds were finally on their way.
"It's extremely dangerous...," Sanderson told reporters at Thredbo, southwest of Sydney in the picturesque Snowy Mountains, Australia's main winter playground.
"The big fear that we have at the moment is that the weather might break. If it rains, that area would be so much more dangerous," he added.
A total of 20 people were believed to have been buried in the landslide, which sent one ski lodge crashing into another below it late on Wednesday night. Ten are still missing.
Investigations into the cause of the slide have focused on groundwater making the heavily developed hillside unstable.

Just before sunrise, one huge boulder moved several centimetres as well as a big concrete slab, under which Diver remarkably survived for about 64 hours in a cramped pocket of air. More victims were believed to be entombed in the same area.
Diver is recovering in a hospital in Canberra, 150 km (90 miles) north of Thredbo, and is reported to be sitting up in bed, having suffered only frostbite and minor cuts.
He was expected to remain in hospital for at least a few days for "extensive treatment", a hospital spokesman said.
